label: Auth
description: Identifies callers before any policy runs, and never decides what they may do. Our own tokens: a sign-in graph verifies a credential against a directory (identity.port.json), then token.port.json#issue signs a short-lived access token and opens a session with a refresh token; on every gated trigger the guard verifies that token -- and nothing a downstream directory issued -- and hands request.principal and request.session to the policies. Sessions carry attributes of the shape settings.session names, written and read through session.port.json. Sessions and challenges are kept through state.port.json, a port this plugin requires and the host binds: to files.port.json for one process, to a store for many. A policy that challenges opens a one-time challenge; challenge.port.json#issue gives it a code, and the guard verifies the code the caller presents. A trigger gives the guard its credentials where it attaches a policy: { "policy": "...", "in": { "token": "{{request.headers.authorization}}" } }.

issuer.description: the iss claim our tokens carry, and the only issuer the guard accepts

secret.description: the HS256 signing key, read from {{secrets.<key>}}; 32 bytes or more

accessTtl.description: seconds an access token lives; default 900

refreshTtl.description: seconds a refresh token, and so a session, lives without refreshing; default 604800

tokens.description: how our tokens are signed and judged

session.description: the shape of a session's attributes: what request.session.attributes reads and session.port.json writes. Absent: attributes are untyped

ttl.description: seconds a challenge stays open; default 300

attempts.description: wrong codes before a challenge is void; default 5

methods.description: method name -> how a caller obtains a code; a policy outcome's method names one

token.description: an access token this plugin issued, read where the kind hands it: {{request.headers.authorization}} (a Bearer prefix is stripped), {{request.cookies.session}}, {{request.flags.token}}; a list is the places it may sit, the first present wins

id.description: the challenge id the caller was told

subject.description: the sub claim: who the directory said this is

realm.description: which sign-in issued the token: what the domain graph wrote (employee, customer)

claims.description: every claim of the verified token

principal.description: the caller our token names; absent when no credential was presented

session.description: the caller's session, opened when the token was issued; its attributes are the shape settings.session names

challenge.description: the challenge the caller answered, its code verified; absent when none was presented

refuses.invalid_credential: a token or a challenge answer was given and did not verify: bad signature, wrong issuer, expired, a session that has ended, an unknown or spent challenge, a wrong code
